title: Callum and the Crooked Claims
markdown:
Callum wasn’t exactly out slaying beasts. He was Callum, the unpaid intern. His big job? Keeping the enchanted quill ink topped up and stopping anyone from losing the really important scrolls. He dreamt of adventure, of course. Who wouldn't, stuck at the Heroic Guild? But mostly, his days were spent sorting through paper. Mountains of it. Each scroll thicker than a troll’s toenail. The ink in his veins felt less like a spark of heroism. More like spilled coffee. He’d stare out the window. Knights clattered by on mighty steeds. He imagined himself on their saddles. But no. His reality? Rustling parchment. Faint, musty prophecies.

Then came Tuesday morning. A whirlwind swept through the Guild hall. Sir Reginald the Ridiculous, the Guild’s star knight, swaggered in. He looked less like he’d fought a dragon and more like he’d wrestled a rainbow. Purple goo clung to his magnificent beard. He smelled faintly of burnt toast and something suspiciously like cheap mead. In his hand, he clutched a scroll. Not a victory scroll. Oh no. This was a scroll of expense claims.

"Right!" Sir Reginald boomed. His voice echoed like a dropped cauldron. "A successful dragon hunt, naturally. Here are the receipts." He plonked the scroll onto Callum’s desk. It landed with a thud that made the inkwells jump. Callum’s eyes widened. The scroll was enormous. It unfurled across his small desk like a monstrous, papery serpent. He picked it up. It felt heavier than a king’s ransom. It probably contained just as much dodgy stuff.

Callum started to sort. His brow furrowed. "One bottle of ‘Dragon Repellent, Extra Sparkly’… Hmm. £500? That seems a bit steep for a bit of fizz." He flipped the page. His fingers were sticky with a trace of the purple goo. "‘Emotional Support Gargoyle Fuel, 3 Gallons’… What in the name of sanity…?" He gulped. His stomach did a wobbly flip. Then came ‘Interdimensional Toll Fees.’ And a truly baffling amount for ‘Dragon-Scale Polishing Cloths, Velvet-Lined.’ Callum paused. A thought dawned. "Here's where it gets interesting," Callum muttered. The dust motes danced in the faint sunlight.

Suddenly, the office temperature plummeted. Not a little chill. A Siberian blizzard kind of drop. The air grew thick and heavy. Like the breath of an approaching ice giant. The door creaked open with an ominous groan. A frigid wind whispered through the hall. Out stepped Petra Grimshaw. Petra the Ledger. Her eyes were like two chips of glacial ice. Sharp. Unyielding. Her smile? As rare as a unicorn’s tax return. Her office was famously colder than a frost giant's handshake. You could hear a misplaced decimal point shiver from fifty paces. Her perfectly tailored suit seemed to soak up all the warmth.

"Callum," Petra’s voice was a frosty whisper. Sharp enough to cut glass. It sent shivers down Callum’s spine. This chill had nothing to do with the air. "Sir Reginald’s quest expenditure. It’s… alarming." She tapped a long, bony finger on a tablet. It glowed with grim numbers. Each one seemed to judge Callum. "We are over budget. Significantly. The Guild’s quarterly review is next week. You will audit these claims. Every. Single. One. Justify this expense, or you will be ‘permanently retired to the archives.’ Understood?"

Permanently retired to the archives. That was Guild-speak for being fired. Buried under a pile of ancient, dusty scrolls. Scrolls untouched since the enchanted printing press. Callum felt a tremor run through him. A cold sweat prickled his brow. This was fear. Pure, unadulterated, soul-shaking fear. He imagined himself lost forever. Amongst forgotten lore. His heroic dreams turned to dust.

That night, Callum stayed late. The Guild hall was silent. Only the faint hum of ancient enchantments. Usually, it lulled everyone to sleep. Now, it whispered secrets in the dark. He pored over the papers. His desk lamp cast long, dancing shadows. He found a hidden clause. In the Guild’s “Heroic Peril Insurance Policy.” It wasn’t insurance. It was a money-laundering scheme. Designed to pay out more to the brokers than the heroes. The broker? A shady character. "Slick" Morty. His name alone sounded like trouble. Wrapped in a dodgy handshake. Callum suspected a conspiracy. Thicker than ogre stew. And a lot less appetizing.

He heard whispers. From Sir Reginald’s stables. Faint, but distinct. Callum peeked through a crack in the weathered wooden door. Sir Reginald wasn't in shining armour. He wore a silken dressing gown. He laughed heartily with Slick Morty. Morty polished a solid gold unicorn horn. "The fools will never notice," Reginald cackled. His voice was a booming, gravelly sound. "That Glimmering Wyrm Scale Polish costs a fortune. But it hides any imperfections, eh, Morty? Makes even a dusty old dragon’s shed scales look like a royal crown!"

Imperfections. Callum’s heart hammered against his ribs. Like a trapped bird. He remembered seeing a discarded bag of that very polish. Near the dragon’s lair. In Reginald’s report. A discarded bag. With a distinctively velvet lining. He snatched it discreetly as he crept away. It was velvet-lined. It smelled faintly of expensive regret. And cheap cologne. He had proof now. Tangible, velvet-lined proof.

The next day was the budget review. Petra sat at the head of the long, polished table. Her gaze was a laser beam. Slicing through any attempt at deception. Sir Reginald, smugly expectant, sat beside her. His golden unicorn horn tucked under his arm. Callum, clutching his evidence, stood before them. His knees wobbled like jelly on a hot griddle. The air in the room was thick with anticipation. And the faint, cloying scent of Sir Reginald's expensive perfume.

"Sir Reginald," Callum began. His voice was small. But surprisingly steady. Like a tiny sprout pushing through concrete. "Your expense report for the Glimmering Wyrm hunt…" He laid out the invoices. The insurance policy details. The velvet-lined polish. He cleared his throat. "The ‘Dragon Repellent’ was just glitter glue. Used to make the dragon look more… festive. The ‘Gargoyle Fuel’ was for Reginald’s pet ferret, Bartholomew. Who apparently enjoys aerial acrobatics. And this polish…" He held up the bag. The velvet glinted under the harsh light. "This polish costs more than three hero salaries combined! It’s not to hide dragon scales. It’s to hide inflated costs. And shoddy work!"

Sir Reginald’s smug face crumpled. Like a discarded biscuit. Slick Morty, who had been lurking in the shadows, trying to blend into the tapestries, attempted to slink away. But Guild guards! Alerted by the commotion. And Callum’s surprisingly loud voice! They nabbed him with practiced efficiency. Petra stared at Callum. For the first time, there was a flicker in her eyes. Something other than ice. A grudging respect, perhaps? Or maybe just surprise. At a junior intern not spontaneously combusting under her gaze.

"Callum," she said. Her voice was still sharp. But with a new, almost imperceptible edge. Not entirely threatening. "You have demonstrated… exceptional fiscal oversight. The Guild will be investigating Sir Reginald and Mr. Morty. And you, Callum… your unpaid internship is hereby… upgraded. To Junior Ledger Clerk. With a small stipend. And dental."

Callum grinned. A wide, ear-to-ear grin. It stretched from one side of his face to the other. It wasn’t exactly dragon-slaying. And it wasn’t rescuing a princess. But for an unpaid intern who’d spent his days buried in paperwork, it felt like a legendary victory. He’d faced down the terrifying Petra Grimshaw. Exposed a crooked knight. He’d saved the Guild’s finances. And his own career. And who knows, maybe one day. With enough experience in expense reports and ledger balancing, he’d finally get to do some adventuring. But for now, the numbers were calling. And for the first time, Callum heard them. Not as a threat. But as a thrilling, exciting challenge. Buckle up, because this part of his career was just beginning! He even managed a small, triumphant wink at Bartholomew the ferret. Who was busy trying to eat the gold unicorn horn.
characters: Callum the unpaid intern at the Heroic Guild, Petra the terrifying chief financial officer
